case_name: Sardarmal Lalwani v State of Madhya Pradesh and Others

statutes.act: Part C Of The Impugned Act

facts: The facts are different but the principles of law to be applied are the same which we have laid down in our judgment in Civil Appeal No. 2139 of 1968.
A new clause was added defining 'Bhopal area'.
The notification to acquire the land in question under s. 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, was published in the Madhya Pradesh Rajpatra, dated October 3, 1962.
Thereafter, the notice under S. 9(1) was published for general information and notices under s. 9(3) were issued to the individual interested parties.
It is alleged inter alia that Bhopal was made Capital of Madhya Pradesh on November 1, 1956.
This report was submitted on September 30, 955.

In view of these facts, it is submitted in ground (viii) of the petition that 'the impugned Act violates Art. 14 of the Constitution as there is no rational classification on the basis of which the prices of Bhopal area have not been determined by the principle by which the market prices of other places would be determined.'

The only reply given to this ground is contained in para 21 of the counter affidavit on behalf of the State wherein it is stated 'With reference to ground (viii), of the petition, I deny that the Amendment Act infringes any- fundamental right of the petitioner and in particular Art. 14 of of the Constitution.'

The learned Advocate General was unable to point out to us any material to show that there was any expectation or speculation on or about the 1st October, 1955 that Bhopal would be the Capital of Madhya Pradesh.
In this case, the acquisition was in 1962 and prices may have risen not only because of speculative dealings but because of general increase in prices throughout the State.
The High Court justified the basis to differentiate the land located in Bhopal area thus :

Now, it cannot be denied that whenever a capital or a big industry is located in a town or even in a city, land values are suddenly pushed up G by prospective sellers and the increase in them during the interregnum between the date when it is known that the town will become more important and the date of acquisition of land may not represent its real value.
The prospect of acquisition of vast areas of private lands in connection, with a capital or industrial project in town always gives rise to speculative dealings in lands in the town.

When such speculative dealings occur it is not unreasonable and improper to compute the market-value of the land with reference to a date proximate to the date of acquisition so as to exclude, speculative rise in determining the market value of the land.

On the material on record, it is impossible for us to hold that in this case there has been a discrimination in the matter of compensation between land acquired in Bhopal area and other areas in the State.

The classification between land in Bhopal area and other parts of the State is with reason and reasonable, and is for the purpose of enabling the State to acquire land at a reasonable price in Bhopal for the construction of the Capital.
In our view, the amendments are not hit by Art. 14 of the Constitution.
There is no material on the record to show that on October 1, 1955, it was known that Bhopal may be the Capital of the State or that there was speculation in land because of this fact.
We have in the judgment delivered in Nagpur movement Trust v. Vithal Rao ([1973] 3 S.C.R. 39 1972 Indlaw SC 421) examined Art. 14 and its implications as far as land acquisition is concerned.
issues: Whether the impugned Act violates Art. 14 of the Constitution as there is no rational classification on the basis of which the prices of Bhopal area have not been determined by the principle by which the market prices of other places would be determined.
Whether the amendments are hit by Art. 14 of the Constitution.
petitioner_arguments: The impugned Act violates Art. 14 of the Constitution as there is no rational classification on the basis of which the prices of Bhopal area have not been determined by the principle by which the market prices of other places would be determined.
There can be no rational basis to differentiate between Bhopal and other areas for award of compensation merely because Bhopal was made Capital.
The theory that in view of Capital, there was speculative prices at Bhopal and the prices at any given time might not reflect the real price, is neither rational nor reasonable.
The date, October 1, 1955, is an arbitrary date for the purpose of fixing the market value.
respondent_arguments: With reference to ground (viii), of the petition, I deny that the Amendment Act infringes any- fundamental right of the petitioner and in particular Art. 14 of of the Constitution.

The classification between land in Bhopal area and other parts of the State is with reason and reasonable, and is for the purpose of enabling the State to acquire land at a reasonable price in Bhopal for the construction of the Capital.
court_reasoning: In our view, the amendments are not hit by Art. 14 of the Constitution.

The classification between land in Bhopal area and other parts of the State is with reason and reasonable, and is for the purpose of enabling the State to acquire land at a reasonable price in Bhopal for the construction of the Capital.
In our view, in the light of that judgment, the petition must be allowed.
The amendments themselves indicate that it was because of the location of the Capital at Bhopal that they had to be made.

Now, it cannot be denied that whenever a capital or a big industry is located in a town or even in a city, land values are suddenly pushed up G by prospective sellers and the increase in them during the interregnum between the date when it is known that the town will become more important and the date of acquisition of land may not represent its real value.
The prospect of acquisition of vast areas of private lands in connection, with a capital or industrial project in town always gives rise to speculative dealings in lands in the town.

When such speculative dealings occur it is not unreasonable and improper to compute the market-value of the land with reference to a date proximate to the date of acquisition so as to exclude, speculative rise in determining the market value of the land.
holding: The petition is allowed with costs and it is declared that section 3 part C of the impugned Act is hit by the provisions of Art. 14 of the Constitution.
